definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X_r=x^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; X_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear operators on V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r! in the universal enveloping algebra and in its action on V; Y_0 is the identity.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl2(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all X_r and Y_r for integers r≥0; its action on V is the given enveloping-algebra action.

definitions.type: family of vectors in V indexed by I

definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}. It is embedded in C through Q.
M_R=R⊗_Z M; tensors use the natural integer-module structures.

definitions.type: R-linear map from M_R to V
definitions.definition: μ:M_R→V is the multiplication map μ(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R,m∈M. Its image is the R-span of M inside V. Identification of M_R with that image is made only after proving injectivity.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I×I
definitions.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero, using the previously proved basis (e_k) of V.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I

definitions.definition: J=J_0, using 0∈I under the original nonnegative range of λ.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, with bracket induced from [h,x]=2x,[h,y]=-2y,[x,y]=h. No assertion that this is a simple Lie algebra in characteristic 2 is made.
x_K(m⊗c)=(xm)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives xM⊆M since x=X_1.
y_K(m⊗c)=(ym)⊗c, for m∈M,c∈K. Admissibility gives yM⊆M since y=Y_1.

inputs.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

n=λ+1>0, I has n elements, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For all integers d≥0, hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^d v, and for d≥1, xy^d v=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. For all d>λ, y^d v=0. For i∈I: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) if i≥1; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ and ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r≤i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise.

μ is injective. Identifying M_R with μ(M_R)⊆V, M_R is free of rank n over R, its complex span is V, and every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves it. For all i,j∈I the integer binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ-i) Y_λ X_λ Y_(λ-j). In particular every E_ij preserves M_R.
There exists a nonzero complex number b∈J such that J=Rb and (b e_i)_{i∈I}, viewed in M_R through the injective map μ, is an R-basis of M_R.

output.statement: n>0 and there exists a K-basis B=(B_i)_{i∈I} of V_K. On this basis x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for 1≤i≤λ; y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ and y_K B_λ=0; h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i. These are exactly the induced actions of x,y,h, so they define the stated L_K-action. All integer coefficients here are mapped into K. For 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K; define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. For i,j∈I let T_ij be the K-linear map B_j↦B_i with all other basis vectors mapped to zero. Then binom(λ,j) is nonzero in K and T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). Moreover A_r,C_r are precisely the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r on V_K.

argument.text: Every integer denominator of an element of R is prime to p, so its image in the characteristic-p field K is nonzero by H001. Thus ρ:R→K, ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), is a well-defined ring map; equality of fractions and the ring laws follow by cross multiplication. Its kernel is pR and its residue field is Z/pZ: ρ(a/b)=0 exactly when p divides a. Define φ: M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse takes (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect all tensor balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors, which span. Also η:z⊗c↦(z mod pM_R)⊗c identifies M_R⊗_R K with (M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K. The inverse sends (z mod pM_R)⊗c to z⊗c; changing z by p times a vector gives zero because pK=0, and all remaining balancing relations follow from ρ. These are the two natural isomorphisms of the supplied proof. H005 gives xM,yM⊆M and H003 gives h=xy-yx, hence hM⊆M. Tensoring these lattice operators commutes with φ and η by their formulas. The induced h equals h_K=x_Ky_K-y_Kx_K. The induced brackets therefore give the L_K-action, including characteristic 2.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K has kernel pR and residue field Z/pZ. The displayed maps φ:V_K≅M_R⊗_R K and η:M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K are K-linear isomorphisms commuting with all induced lattice-preserving operators. In particular x_K,y_K,h_K are the induced actions of x,y,h and give the L_K-action.

argument.text: Choose b from N004 and define B_i=φ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1). The R-coordinate isomorphism M_R≅R^I given by the basis (b e_i) tensors to K^I; tensoring its coordinate maps gives inverse coefficient maps, proving that B is a K-basis, not merely a spanning family. Alternatively its reduction is a basis of M_R/pM_R over Z/pZ and then extends to K, via F001. N001 gives the matrices of x,y,h on e_i, and complex linearity gives the same matrices on b e_i. Their coefficients are integers, so extension along ρ and transport by φ give exactly x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for i≥1, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i, with integer coefficients read in K. Also n>0 by N001.

produces.statement: n>0 and B=(B_i)_{i∈I} is a K-basis of V_K, with x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for 1≤i≤λ, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i.

argument.text: For every r with 0≤r≤λ<p, none of 1,...,r is divisible by p, so r! is nonzero in K by H001. Define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. On M the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold; all these operators preserve M by H005. After extension they show that the induced X_r,Y_r are exactly A_r,C_r. For i,j∈I, N002 expresses E_ij as a composition of R-lattice operators and the unit binom(λ,j)^(-1). Its extension, transported by φ, sends B_j to B_i and every other B-coordinate to zero, hence is the map T_ij defined from F002. The image of that unit under ρ remains a unit and is the inverse of the coefficient binom(λ,j) in K, so this coefficient is nonzero. Substituting the just established induced divided powers in N002 gives T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). This proves every exported clause of the output without comparing reduced weights.
